taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Market-road (Bori Metropolis). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 104 | 2.86 | 2.86
2 | 186 | 2.38 | 5.24
3 | 266 | 24.7 | 29.9
4 | 327 | 24.6 | 54.6
5 | 219 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as AAA-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: Market-road (Bori Metropolis)
Curve type: AAK (recalculated from the resistivity sequence 104→186→266→327→219; the file’s “AAA” label is inconsistent with the data, as the 3rd triplet 266<327>219 is a K, not an A)
Aquifer depth: 29.9 m – 54.6 m (high-resistivity Layer 4, likely coarse sand/gravel)
Recommendation: Advance the borehole through the upper clayey/sandy overburden (0–29.9 m) with temporary casing, and target screen placement within the 29.9–54.6 m interval; confirm lithology by cuttings before finalizing screen depth, as the underlying Layer 5 (219 Ω·m) may indicate a transition to finer, less productive material.
